Course structure

Lectures Focus Topics
L1–L4 Foundations The data science workflow, linear algebra, probability and statistics, applications, data quality, and preprocessing.
L5–L7 Learning from data Regression, classification, unsupervised learning, and embeddings, with emphasis on evaluation and generalization.
L8–L9 Modern AI Deep learning, foundation models, LLMs, and agentic systems for interactive data science applications.

Learning outcomes

By the end of the course, students should be able to:

  • Formulate a data science problem and build a reproducible analysis workflow.
  • Prepare and visualize data, and interpret uncertainty and statistical evidence.
  • Select, fit, and evaluate supervised and unsupervised models on unseen data.
  • Explain learned representations and the core mechanisms of deep learning and foundation models.
  • Use AI agents effectively, verify their outputs, and communicate and defend the results.

Assessment

Weight Component Details
10% Attendance and participation Starting from Week 2.
35% Homework assignments Approximately every two weeks; 3–4 assignments in total.
25% Midterm exam October 21, 2026, in class. Closed book; approximately 1.5–2 hours. One A4 cheat sheet and a calculator permitted.
30% Group project Three members per group. Collaborate with AI agents and evaluate the resulting work. Report and presentations in November.

Group project milestones

  • Report deadline: November 17, 2026, at 11:59 PM.
  • Presentations: November 18 and November 25, approximately 10 minutes per group.

Project resources:

  • Group project assessment guide
  • Presentation guide
  • Report templates (LaTeX, Word)
  • Peer review system

Acknowledgments

This course was originally created and taught by Prof. Yanchao Yang from 2024 through Spring 2026.

The modern AI portions draw extensively on materials from MIT 6.7960 Deep Learning, Caltech EE/CS 148B Large Language & Vision Models, and Stanford CS146S The Modern Software Developer.
